newsitem.title: USA: Leslie-ADM pegs US corn 9.221 bln bu, soy 2.38 bln.
newsitem.headline: Leslie-ADM pegs US corn 9.221 bln bu, soy 2.38 bln.

text.p: The Conrad Leslie-ADM Elevator survey on Friday estimated U.S. corn production based on Nov 1 conditions at 9,221,411,000 bushels and soybeans at 2,383,737,000 bushels, versus the 8,906,484,000 bu corn and 2,302,329,000 bu soybeans Leslie estimated last month.
The estimates are based on inquiries with 1,200 grain elevators in the Corn Belt.

The estimates compare with U.S. Agriculture Department's Oct 1 estimates of 9,012,148,000 bu corn and 2,346,220,000 bu soybeans. U.S. corn production in 1995 totaled 7,373,876,000 bu and soybeans 2,151,834,000 bu.
U.S. average production for the past five years has been 8,152,954,000 bu corn and 2,143,000,000 bu soybeans.

Leslie pegged average corn yield at 125.9 bushels per acre against last month's estimate of 121.6 bushels an acre, the five-year average of 118.6 bu and last year's 113.5 bu. The record corn yield of 138.6 bu per acre was set in 1994.

Leslie said the corn crop was 63 percent harvested Nov 1 against the usual pace of 71 percent, indicating that about 3.4 billion bushels remain in the fields. But better yields than expected a month ago were reported in Indiana, Illinois, Iowa, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Nebraska and Missouri, he said.

Leslie sharply raised his estimate for end-season corn carryout for Aug 31, 1997, to 1.102 billion bushels from 777 million bushels estimated last month. This would represent a jump of 158 percent from 426 million bu on Aug 31, 1996.

Leslie also raised his estimate of end-season stocks of soybeans on Aug 31, 1997, to 227 million bushels compared to 200 million seen last month and 183 million on Aug 31, 1996, based on current demand estimates by USDA.
Leslie pegged average soybean yield at 37.6 bushels an acre against last month's estimate of 36.3 bushels, the five-year average of 36.1 and last year's 34.9 bushels.
The record U.S. soybean yield was 41.4 bu/acre in 1994.
Leslie said soybean harvest on Nov 1 was 80 percent complete compared to normal progress of 87 percent, indicating about 480 million bushels remain in the fields.
But better yields were reported in the last month by elevators in Indiana, Illinois, Iowa, Nebraska and Missouri, Leslie said.
